is asserted without one. `approx: true` marks a date the sources disagree on
or give only to the month; the UI shows those differently.

this one was framed as a response to, which is what draws the

situations.name: US–Israel–Iran War
situations.summary: Seventh month of war. A June memorandum halted large-scale fighting, but both sides trade strikes over alleged violations. Iran's nuclear program, control of the Strait of Hormuz, and sanctions relief all remain unresolved.
watch: Strait of Hormuz transit and minelaying
US shift from bombing to financial pressure

timeline.action: Trump authorises Operation Epic Fury, the joint US–Israeli campaign against Iran.
Coordinated opening strikes — Tomahawks, B-2s and fighters against military facilities, command centres and a leadership compound in Tehran. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is killed.
Roughly 170 ballistic missiles and drones fired at Israel, Gulf states and US bases.
timeline.where: Israel, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain

timeline.action: Rocket attacks on an IDF base at Haifa. Israel calls it a declaration of war.
Airstrikes against more than 70 targets in Lebanon.
Largest single day of the campaign — 104 reported strikes, including the Natanz nuclear facility. Iranian naval vessels destroyed in the Gulf; the corvette IRIS Shahid Soleimani is sunk.
Khamenei's successor is elected.
Naval blockade of Iranian ports begins. DoD estimates $4.8bn in lost Iranian oil revenue by 1 May.
Airstrikes on military sites in southern Iran and Tehran, during the ceasefire, in response to Iranian targeting of US warships.
Pakistan-mediated ceasefire and memorandum of understanding halt large-scale fighting. Sources place this in June; the exact date is unsettled.
Treasury announces expanded sanctions, described by Secretary Bessent as the most crushing economic operation ever mounted.
Qatar-mediated negotiations over Strait of Hormuz access.

US strikes two IRGC launchers on Larak Island after forces were observed preparing to lay sea mines in the strait. CENTCOM calls it limited, precise action — the first US strike on Iran in over a month.
IRGC launches missiles and drones it calls "Punishment of the Aggressor" at the King Hussein and Al Azraq bases in Jordan, and at Al Minhad airbase in the UAE.

situations.name: Gaza War
situations.summary: In its third year, and eleven months into a ceasefire that has held without ending the killing. Phase Two — disarmament, reconstruction and a technocratic administration — was declared in January 2026, but no comprehensive rebuilding has begun, the committee meant to run Gaza has not been allowed to enter, and the Yellow Line still bisects the Strip.
watch: Whether Phase Two moves beyond declaration
Entry of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza
Reconstruction access and the Yellow Line
Aid funding — agencies are cutting programmes
Winter: shelter, water and disease as the rainy season arrives
situations.indicatorNote: No market is linked to this subject. The meaningful indicators here are humanitarian — shelter, aid volume, water, casualties — and none of them are available as a live feed, so none are charted rather than substituting a financial proxy.

sources.label: A Guide to the Gaza Peace Deal (CFR)
Six months into the ceasefire (Al Jazeera)
UN Security Council on the ceasefire

timeline.action: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel. The war begins.
Israeli ground invasion of the Gaza Strip begins.
First truce takes effect, with hostage and prisoner exchanges.
Israeli offensive on Rafah begins, displacing much of the population sheltering in the south.
The January 2025 ceasefire takes effect.
Israel resumes large-scale strikes; the January ceasefire collapses.

The current ceasefire takes effect after the Israeli cabinet approves the agreement. Israeli forces withdraw to the Yellow Line, which bisects the Strip and leaves the population in under half its territory.
More than twenty world leaders gather at Sharm el-Sheikh, where Trump signs the agreement ending the two-year war.
The Security Council endorses the agreement, which enters into force as Resolution 2803.
Israel confirms Hamas has returned the remains of the last hostage taken on 7 October 2023, fulfilling the terms of Phase One. Sources place this in January; the exact date is unsettled.
The US announces the transition to Phase Two: disarming Hamas, rebuilding the territory, and standing up a committee of Palestinian experts to administer daily affairs under American supervision.
Six months into the ceasefire, reporting describes neither war nor peace — continued Israeli attacks, no tangible recovery, and no comprehensive reconstruction begun.
Tallies through this date record 1,259 people killed and 4,146 injured in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025.

The Security Council is told the ceasefire, though far from perfect, remains the basis for recovery: some 80 per cent of buildings are damaged or destroyed, more than a million people lack permanent shelter, and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza has still not been allowed to enter. The meeting date is approximate.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine War
situations.summary: Fifth year of full-scale war. Three rounds of US-brokered talks through the spring produced prisoner exchanges and a brief energy ceasefire but never reached the territorial question. Moscow declared negotiations at a dead end in late August and is escalating strikes on Kyiv.
watch: Whether talks resume or Russia formalises the escalation
Strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure ahead of winter
Ukrainian deep strikes on Russian refineries

timeline.action: Russia launches the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Russian forces withdraw from the Kyiv region after failing to take the capital, and atrocities at Bucha come to light. Sources give the withdrawal over several days in early April.
Mariupol falls after a destructive siege, completing Russia's land bridge to Crimea.
Ukraine's Kharkiv counteroffensive breaks the front and recaptures territory, forcing a Russian retreat.
Russia declares the annexation of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts.
Ukrainian forces liberate Kherson city, the only regional capital Russia had captured.
Russia captures Bakhmut after the longest and deadliest battle of the war.
The Kakhovka Dam is destroyed, flooding communities along the Dnieper and draining the reservoir. Responsibility is disputed.
Wagner forces under Prigozhin mutiny and advance toward Moscow before turning back.
Avdiivka falls to Russian forces after a prolonged battle, Russia's most significant gain since Bakhmut.
Ukraine launches a cross-border incursion into Russia's Kursk Oblast, the first major ground operation on Russian soil.

Russia and Ukraine hold direct talks in Istanbul for the first time in three years. They end in under two hours with no ceasefire, but agree to exchange 1,000 prisoners each — the largest swap of the war.
A second Istanbul round exchanges memorandums setting out each side's peace terms, without agreement.
US and Ukrainian negotiators agree a 20-point plan to end the war, which passes to Moscow for review. Sources place this in December; the exact date is unsettled.
Starlink service is cut off for Russian forces operating in Ukraine, degrading their tactical communications.

Ukraine launches a counteroffensive on the southern front in the Oleksandrivka and Hulyaipole directions, aiming to expel Russian forces from Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and disrupt Russia's planned spring offensive. It produces the first monthly net Ukrainian territorial gain since the 2024 Kursk incursion.
Ukraine announces the results of the Oleksandrivka counteroffensive covering January to August 2026, its largest offensive inside the country since 2023.
Drone strike on hotels at Khorly kills 28 civilians during New Year celebrations.
Oreshnik hypersonic missile strike on Lviv.
Russian forces cross the international border into Sumy Oblast and claim the seizure of Komarivka.
First trilateral Russia–US–Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, covering disengagement of forces and ceasefire monitoring. A prisoner exchange of 314 people is completed.
Putin agrees to halt strikes on Kyiv until 1 February following a request from Trump.
Strike severely damages the Darnytsia thermal power station, cutting heat and power in the capital.
Russian forces capture Myrnohrad and Svitle.
Second Abu Dhabi round produces a one-week energy ceasefire under US pressure, but leaves territory unresolved.
Geneva round puts the territorial question on the agenda for the first time.
A further Abu Dhabi round ends without result. Sources place this in early March; the exact date is unsettled.
Ukrainian deep strikes hit an oil refinery in Leningrad Oblast and a warehouse in Tver Oblast overnight.
Russia launches 112 drones against Ukraine overnight. Lavrov rules out any ceasefire that freezes the current front line.
Putin moves to escalate the war after concluding that negotiations have reached a dead end, weighing intensified ballistic missile attacks on central Kyiv and infrastructure elsewhere.
The Kremlin says peace talks are on a "deep pause" as Russian troops press the offensive in the east.
At least 12 people are killed in and around Kyiv on the sixth consecutive night of drone attacks. Zelenskyy says Moscow is exploiting a shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors.
